To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the liquid-phase peptide synthesis using the soluble polymer support, 4- (aminomethyl)- 3-nitro-benzoyl-amino- poly(ethylene glycol), was successful for the synthesis of the mast cell degranulation tetradecapeptides.

The liquid-phase synthesis was used to prepare three mast cell degradulating peptides from wasp venom, and the photolysis method was used to cleave the completed peptideamids from the poly(ethylene glycol).

the liquid-phase synthesis of peptides is feasible, that the 4-(aminobenzoyl)-aminopoly(ethylene glycol)-supported peptide synthesis is a useful approach for the synthesis of peptides, and that the photolysis method for cleavage of peptideamides from the polyethylene glycol support is effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of peptides of biological interest by the liquid-phase method.
the liquid-phase synthesis of naturally-occurring peptides and polypeptides, using soluble polymeric supports.
the synthesis of naturally occurring peptide amides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the liquid phase method of peptide synthesis, using the 4-aminomethyl-3-nitro-benzoic acid polymer support, is a useful technique for the synthesis of biologically active peptides, and that the technique has been applied successfully to the synthesis of three mast cell-degranulating tetradeca peptide amides from wasps.

the present liquid-phase syntheses of three mast-cell degranulating tetra-decapeptide amides from the wasp venom peptides, mastoparan, Mastoparan X, Polistes Mastopar-an, have been successfully accomplished.

the present liquid-phase method of peptide synthesis is capable of producing peptides of a size comparable to the mast cell degranulators described herein, and is a promising technique for the synthesis of larger peptides and proteins, provided that a soluble support can be devised which is compatible with the photolysis conditions and which can be cleaved from the completed peptide in high yield.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 4-(aminobenzyl)-3-nitrophenoxy-protected amino-poly(ethylene)glycol is a very useful soluble support for liquid-phase synthesis of peptide amides.
liquid-phase synthesis of naturally-occurring peptides is a viable alternative to the solid-phase method.

the use of photolysis as a means for cleaving the peptideamides from the support is effective for the synthesis of peptides containing tryptophan and histidine, and the use of 4-(aminobenzoyl-amino)-poly(ethylene glycol)-monomethyl ether as the soluble support is effective for synthesizing peptides containing the amino acids with the side-chain functional groups that are not readily protected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photolysis method is a viable means of cleaving the completed peptide from the support, and is applicable to peptides containing labile amino acids.
the liquid-phase peptide synthesis can be carried out in a manner that is compatible with the biological activities of the products.
it is feasible to synthesize peptides containing a large number of basic amino acid residues by the liquid-phase method.
